name: Constant Contact
tagline: Send simple newsletters, manage contacts, and publish signup forms

tiers.name: Lite

tiers.notes: Live page showed current selector/promo price; price varies with contacts and email sends.

tiers.notes: Live page showed current selector/promo price; price varies with contacts and email sends.

tiers.notes: Live page showed current selector/promo price; price varies with contacts and email sends.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; trial/start flow only, no ongoing free caps verified.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly pricing shown; annual discount not verified on crawled official page
pricing.hiddenCosts: Plan cost scales with contact count and email-send multiples; SMS add-on starts at $10/mo with first 500 messages/month; Inbox Preview add-on $10/mo.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Constant Contact, send simple newsletters, manage contacts, and publish signup forms. The hard boundary is deliverability, templates, event and social tools, integrations, and support, plus deliverability, growth network, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Collect subscribers through signup forms, compose and send simple compliant newsletters, manage contacts, publish a web archive, and report basic delivery and click events.
whatYouLose: deliverability, templates, event and social tools, integrations, and support
ongoingBurden: DNS authentication, reputation, bounces, complaints, unsubscribe compliance, templates, queues, analytics, backups, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Constant Contact because newsletter operators pay for inbox placement, growth mechanics, and operational confidence on publication day. The recurring cost buys DNS authentication, reputation, bounces, complaints, unsubscribe compliance, templates, queues, analytics, backups, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Listmonk
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source newsletter and mailing-list manager.

alternatives.name: Brevo Free
alternatives.desc: Simple campaigns, contacts and forms with a 300-email daily ceiling.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, campaigns, consent records, and message events live in Brevo's cloud; contacts can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Brevo Free covers campaigns, contacts, and forms, but its 300-message daily ceiling and lighter beginner hand-holding make it less forgiving than Constant Contact.
facts.setupBlocker: Authenticating a custom sending domain requires adding DNS records.

alternatives.name: EmailOctopus Free
alternatives.desc: A small list, campaigns and one form without a bill; automation and reporting limits are clearly visible.

facts.dataFormat: Lists, campaigns, automations, and reporting data live in EmailOctopus' cloud; contacts and reports can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: EmailOctopus Free is clean for a small list, but its limited forms, automation count, and short reporting window trail Constant Contact's broader small-business toolkit.
facts.setupBlocker: You must verify a sender address or domain; DNS authentication is the first technical step.

alternatives.name: Keila
alternatives.desc: Self-hosted newsletters and signup forms with a real visual editor; SMTP setup replaces onboarding calls.

facts.install: Keila Cloud signup or Docker image plus PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted subscribers, campaigns, and job state live in PostgreSQL; uploaded campaign assets live on persistent server storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Keila replaces newsletters and signup forms, but SMTP authentication, deliverability, server maintenance, backups, and upgrades replace Constant Contact's guided hosted setup.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, PostgreSQL, a public HTTPS domain, and credentials for SMTP, SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, or Postmark.

alternatives.name: Kit Free
alternatives.desc: Forms, landing pages and unlimited sends for creators; the editor is less event-flyer, more newsletter.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, tags, forms, broadcasts, sequences, purchases, and analytics live in Kit's cloud; subscriber and chart data export as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Kit Free offers excellent forms and newsletters for creators, but its creator-first editor and workflows are less suited to event promotions and general small-business campaigns than Constant Contact.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no software install, but custom-domain sending requires DNS authentication and the free plan keeps one Kit-managed recommendation slot.

alternatives.name: listmonk
alternatives.desc: Lists, campaigns and embeddable forms in a fast admin; hand-holding is not bundled.

facts.install: Docker Compose or a single release binary plus PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, templates, and analytics live in a PostgreSQL database on your server.
facts.gapVsPaid: listmonk handles lists, campaigns, and embeddable forms, but it offers much less onboarding, design assistance, and small-business hand-holding than Constant Contact.
facts.setupBlocker: You still need a PostgreSQL database and a trustworthy SMTP/API sender with authenticated DNS.

alternatives.name: Sender Free
alternatives.desc: Newsletters, contact management and signup forms for 2,500 subscribers; branding is the free-tier watermark.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, automations, and engagement events live in Sender's cloud; subscriber data can be exported.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sender Free covers newsletters, contacts, and forms, but vendor branding and free-plan account limits are the price of replacing Constant Contact.
facts.setupBlocker: A custom sending domain must be verified with DNS records for reliable delivery.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Lite plan and a single-publication newsletter DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Constant Contact in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Amazon SES; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect subscribers through signup forms, compose and send simple compliant newsletters, manage contacts, publish a web archive, and report basic delivery and click events.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement subscriber import, double opt-in, unsubscribe, suppression, tags, and consent timestamps.
Create a Markdown campaign editor with HTML and plain-text previews.
Queue sends through SES with retries, rate limits, idempotency, and resumable batches.
Process delivery, bounce, complaint, open, and click webhooks without logging message content.
Publish a simple issue archive and subscriber preference page.
Add test sends, seed-list checks, DNS setup guidance, exports, and backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a newsletter recommendation marketplace.
Deliberately leave out ad sales and payment infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out complex lifecycle automation and enterprise deliverability support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
